title: Re-contextualizing Fairness in NLP: The Case of India
findings: Sentiment analysis models showed negative associations for Muslim and Hindu identities, while having positive associations for Jain and Christian identities. Stereotypical associations for religious groups (e.g., 'Muslim' with 'terrorist' or 'butcher', 'Hindu' with 'pandit') were found to be preferentially encoded in corpora (IndicCorp-en, Wikipedia) and language models (mBERT, MuRIL). The India-specific model, MuRIL, showed a higher percentage of stereotypical predictions compared to mBERT, suggesting it learned more stereotypes from its India-sourced training data.
references: Abubakar Abid, Maheen Farooqi, and James Zou. 2021. Persistent anti-muslim bias in large language models.
